description:
We are building EarthSageAI, an autonomous Earth science research platform for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. Our goal is to analyze real NASA Earth observation datasets, identify environmental trends, perform statistical significance testing, and visualize scientific findings through interactive maps and evidence-backed reports.

We are looking for passionate teammates with interests in Earth Science, GIS, Statistics, Data Analysis, Data Visualization, Ai ML who want build meaningful together.
summary:
EarthSage AI is an AI-assisted Earth system trend analysis platform that helps users explore and understand long-term climate patterns using NASA Earth observation data. Developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge, it uses NASA POWER monthly climate data to analyze temperature and precipitation trends for Lahore, Pakistan, from 1991 to 2020.

The platform applies statistical methods such as the Mann-Kendall test and Sen's slope to identify long-term trends, detect anomalies, and explain significant changes in climate variables. It combines scientific calculations with AI-generated explanations to make complex climate information easier to understand.

EarthSage AI aims to make climate data more accessible, support evidence-based environmental awareness, and help users explore how local climate conditions have changed over time.
details:
EarthSage AI is a web-based climate trend analysis platform designed to help users understand long-term changes in Earth's climate system through accessible data exploration.

The project uses NASA POWER monthly climate data for Lahore, Pakistan, covering 1991–2020. It analyzes temperature variables (T2M, T2M_MAX, T2M_MIN) and precipitation (PRECTOTCORR). Users can explore historical patterns, identify anomalies, and investigate statistically significant trends.

The scientific analysis uses methods including the Mann-Kendall trend test, Sen's slope estimator, autocorrelation checks, and anomaly detection. These methods help distinguish meaningful long-term patterns from ordinary variation. AI-assisted explanations make the statistical findings easier to understand and provide research directions based on the results.

The platform follows an evidence-first approach: statistical calculations are performed by the scientific analysis engine, while the AI component assists with explanations and research planning. It does not present historical analysis as a future climate forecast or make unsupported causal claims.

Technology stack:
Frontend: React and TypeScript

Backend: Python and FastAPI

Database: PostgreSQL with Neon

Scientific analysis: NumPy, SciPy, Statsmodels, and PyMannKendall

AI: Google Gemini API

Deployment: Vercel and Render

The project aims to make NASA climate data easier to explore, understand, and communicate, encouraging evidence-based climate awareness at the local level.
